question: Does actual multiprocessing spawn startup, delayed immediately before Process.start(), add its duration to cancellation response and pause the standard MCP event loop?
runtime: Windows host; Python 3.11 multiprocessing spawn; repository Fake X owned-session fixture; helper workers return synthetic disconnect/UNKNOWN receipts; no X server, Xlib server operation, physical input, WSL, WSLc, Docker, or external model

actual-spawn-no-delay.expectation: both real helper processes are created and retired; cleanup is UNKNOWN; response and heartbeat gaps include actual Windows spawn cost

actual-spawn-with-delay.expectation: both helper starts sleep in the caller process immediately before the real Process.start(); response and heartbeat gaps include at least the two injected delays plus actual spawn cost; cleanup is UNKNOWN

frozen_inputs.action: one CTRL+a chord; Fake X owner blocks in sync until parent retirement
frozen_inputs.disconnect_helper: real spawned process returns a synthetic disconnected receipt
frozen_inputs.release_helper: real spawned process returns a synthetic unknown receipt and emits no input

measurements: public interface_guarded_cancel elapsed_ms from call entry through return
maximum asyncio heartbeat gap spanning cancellation
per-helper Process.start wrapper delay, clean helper exit code and retirement
cancel/release/terminal UNKNOWN metadata and replay denial

decision.evidence_rule: All six trials must show exactly two helper starts, clean worker retirement, release_confirmed=false, cleanup UNKNOWN, task_success=null and replay_allowed=false. Delayed-arm response and event-loop gap must exceed the no-delay arm.
decision.scope_limit: The helper receipt is synthetic. This proves only caller/process-start timing composition, not XRes wire behavior, real release, physical input, OS hard bounds, or the proposed supervisor architecture.
